title: Hosted SSE: orphaned-chunk handoff + session cleanup to prevent partial outputs after mid-response throttling
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers reported truncated or partially duplicated responses after a mid-response quota throttle or transient TCP disconnect. Root cause appears to be a combination of (a) connection termination at the edge LB during hosted quota enforcement, which leaves the runtime with in-flight chunk fragments; and (b) our current session-handoff logic which can mark a session closed before all fragments are durably attributed, resulting in orphaned chunks that are either lost or replayed on a subsequent session leading to partial outputs and duplicate tokens.

Observed customer symptoms: customers see streamed responses end abruptly with no final 'done' event; some clients receive duplicated suffix tokens when the client reconnects and the server retries; a few show manifestly truncated JSON tool-calls. This has triggered three P0 escalations in the last month (Zendesk #ZD-98431, #ZD-99210, #ZD-100123).

Hypothesis: When hosted quota throttling triggers an edge-driven connection kill, the edge returns a 429/terminate ABI but data buffered in runtime's output queue may not have been checkpointed. Our session fencing marks the session as closed when the final ack handshake fails, but there is no durable orphan reconciliation step that inspects partial token_sequence ranges and either backfills or emits an explicit EndOfStream marker. Additionally, the handoff token used by the runtime to reassign chunk ownership is currently 64-bit non-monotonic and may collide across high churn, making reconciliation ambiguous for busy tenants.

Scope & impact: Affects hosted API streaming (SSE/HTTP chunked) only. Estimated impacted traffic: ~0.6% of streaming requests during high-throttle windows; concentrated on customers who use very long responses and rely on strict structural output (embeds + JSON tool-calls). Severity: high (customer-visible corruption / truncation).

Acceptance criteria / success metrics: 
- No customer-reported truncated final tokens in canary region for 72 hours after rollout.
- stream.orphaned_chunks and stream.handoff_retries emit and alert when rate > 0.1% of streaming requests in a 5m window.
- Addition of an explicit durable EndOfStream marker to the SSE framing when runtime detects edge-driven termination; clients that ignore marker should continue to work.

Proposed fix (high-level):
1) Streaming framing: append an explicit durable EOS marker event (framing: event: eos, data: {session_id, last_sequence}) emitted from runtime to the edge when the runtime believes it has no more tokens to emit, and persist a tiny session checkpoint to the session index before emitting. This makes the intent explicit even if the TCP connection is reset after the write is queued.
2) Session fencing + handoff: change handoff token to a monotonic local_epoch + session_epoch tuple and persist it with the session checkpoint. Add an idempotent check on handoff accept that verifies last_sequence and checksum of tail chunk.
3) Orphan reconciler: background worker that scans session index for sessions in TERMINATING state older than X seconds and attempts either (a) reconstruct final fragment by replaying cached token fragments into a short-lived reconciliation run or (b) emit a synthetic EOS marker to downstream monitoring & client-facing analytics.
4) Telemetry and alerts: new metrics stream.orphaned_chunks, stream.reconciliations, stream.eos_emitted, and an SLO alert when orphaned_chunks > 0.1%.

Rollback plan: feature gate controlled via runtime flag enable_eos_marker. Canary rollout to 5% of traffic in us-west-2 for 48 hours. If user-facing errors increase or p95 latency increases > 15% for streaming, flip feature gate off and revert runtime image.

Testing / QA plan: unit tests for monotonic handoff token, integration tests that simulate edge 429-driven connection kills with network-sim (tc/netem) to validate EOS emission, and end-to-end test that verifies no duplicated tokens when a reconnect occurs and handoff occurs mid-response. Add a new test harness case in the streaming regression suite: 'throttle-then-reconnect' including both JSON tool-call and plain text streams.

Notes / Links: see reproduction harness and customer logs in links below.
comments: 2026-02-22 Asha Patel: Triage created after ZD-98431. Assigned to Miguel. Priority set to P0 due to customer-impacting data corruption.

2026-02-23 Miguel Santos: Initial investigation — replicated truncation locally by simulating edge-initiated connection kill while runtime had 3 queued chunks. Observed no persisted checkpoint for the final sequence. Captured runtime logs and chunk checksums. Attaching minimal reproducer script.

2026-02-26 Priya Narang (PM): Confirmed downstream customer sees truncated JSON tool-call that breaks parsing. Requested telemetry counters and escalation comms. Set release target runtime-1.22-canary.

2026-03-01 Miguel Santos: Implemented prototype EOS marker and monotonic handoff epoch. Unit tests passing locally. Running integration suite on staging (staging-hosted-2). Observed one reconciliation attempt failed due to race on session index writes — need atomic checkpoint write.

2026-03-04 Elena Kuznetsova (SRE): Added temp alert on stream.orphaned_chunks > 0.5%. Investigated high watermark windows and correlated with quota-enforcement jobs. Recommend throttle smoothing at edge while runtime fix deploys.

2026-03-08 Miguel Santos: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4218 (proto & reconciler). Requesting code review from Fernando and Rachna. Integration tests in CI are flaky on reconcilier timing; adding backoff & jitter.

2026-03-10 Miguel Santos: Addressed review feedback, added idempotent handoff accept check. Preparing canary deployment: runtime-1.22.3-canary. Scheduling 5% canary in us-west-2 on 2026-03-11. Notifying impacted account owners and support teams.
2026-03-11 Support note: Customer comms prepared — outline of what happened, expected mitigation, and follow-up monitoring. Provide rollback window and contact on-call if any new corruption observed.
2026-03-12 Miguel Santos: Canary deployed to 5% — initial metrics: stream.eos_emitted = 124 over 1h, stream.orphaned_chunks decreased 87% vs baseline. Continuing monitoring for 72h.

2026-03-14 Miguel Santos: Canary shows stable metrics; scheduling region expansion. Plan to close ENG ticket after full rollout and short postmortem document created referencing ENG-137247 (postmortem doc).
